newsitem.title: ESTONIA: INTERVIEW - TALINVEST VOUCHER FUND EYES LATVIA/LITHUANIA.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - TALINVEST VOUCHER FUND EYES LATVIA/LITHUANIA.

text.p: The Estonian Voucher Investment Fund is going to increase the share of Latvian and Lithuanian investments in its portfolio to almost 80 percent from the present 30 percent, the company said on Monday.
"The main idea is to start participating in the Latvian and Lithuanian privatisation process," Sven Soosaar, the managing director of EstIB-Talinvest Asset Management, told Reuters.
"Latvian and Lithuanian companies are more undervalued and we see a larger profit margin there," he added.
Estonia currently counts for about half of the fund's investment portfolio but its stake will decrease to 20 percent for Latvia and Lithuania by the end of the year, Soosaar said.
The fund is going to focus more on Latvia this year but wants to expand its activities to Lithuania over the following years, he added.
The fund is interested in strategic investments.
"The main interest is in companies to be privatised through privatisation vouchers," Soosaar said.
He also mentioned other sectors, such as insurance, which have not achieved their right value yet.

The fund's parent company Talinvest is active in all three Baltic countries, which gives the fund advantages in getting information and opportunities to take part in the privatisation process, he added.
"Latvia is politically more unstable than Estonia but has more potential," Soosaar added.
The fund will issue 388.157 new shares to raise its share capital from present eight million kroons to 16 million kroons. The subscription period is May 19 to June 1, he added.
By the end of the year, the fund plans to issue more shares to raise its capital to 72 million kroons, Soosaar said.
The fund will seek a listing on the stock exchange after having issued new shares, registered itself under a new name and formed its new investment strategy, Soosaar said.
The fund made a profit of nine million kroons last year, which it plans to pay out as dividends.
